content: To access the main page, click here. Introduction to the Electrocardiogram Page The title of the page should follow the format (Disease name) electrocardiogram, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. The purpose of this page is to provide a detailed description and examples of key electrocardiographic (ECG) findings that may be observed in the disease being described. At the top of the edit box, include the following elements: {{CMG}}, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template you created at the beginning. Ensure that you create internal links within WikiDoc by enclosing key terms in brackets. These links should be as specific as possible. For instance, if a sentence includes the term anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. Follow the formatting and capitalization guidelines outlined in the provided template. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. Overview The overview section must include the disease name in the first sentence. The objective of this section is to summarize the ECG findings in a few sentences. This section can mirror the ECG segment from the overview page. For an example of an overview section on an electrocardiogram page, click here. Template First Sentences Preferred Template Statements: If there are no ECG findings associated with the disease: There are no ECG findings associated with [Disease Name]. If an ECG is useful for diagnosis: An ECG may be helpful in the diagnosis of [Disease Name]. If there are specific findings: Findings on an ECG suggestive of/diagnostic of [Disease Name] include [specific findings]. Key ECG Findings in (Disease Name) Provide visual examples of ECG patterns associated with the disease being described. Recommended sources for images include RadsWiki, the National Library of Medicine, Wikipedia, or Radiopaedia. For assistance with inserting images, click here. No Findings or Indications For conditions where an ECG is not indicated, write: There are no clear indications to obtain an ECG in patients with [Disease Name]. For conditions with no associated ECG findings, write: [Disease Name] is not associated with specific ECG findings, and an ECG may not be helpful in the diagnosis or management of this condition. Checklist ECG examples should follow this order: description, image, source, and a line break. The description of the image should clearly convey the condition and include hyperlinks for key terms to enhance searchability. Provide detailed descriptions of key ECG findings, including heart rate, rhythm, segment changes, and special waves (e.g., delta waves in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome). If the image lacks a description, use the name of the image. The ECG image size should be 800 pixels. If this size is too large for the template, reduce it to 500 pixels. Cite source information for the images as shown in the example provided. If there are more than four ECG examples for a single disease, create a separate page titled [Disease Name] ECG examples. Additionally, add an indented tab under the electrocardiogram section in the microchapter navigation template for this page. Provide references for all uploaded ECG images.
